text: Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, "These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do:
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day shall be holy for you, a sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.
You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day."
Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring it as the LORD's offering: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats' hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.
Let everyone among you who is skilled come and make everything the LORD has commanded:

versions.text: Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew חֲכַם־לֵב ("wise of heart") is not gender-specific, and later in this chapter skilled women also take part in the work (vv. 25-26). "Craftsman" narrows the sense unnecessarily; a gender-neutral rendering is more accurate and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: the tabernacle with its tent and covering, its clasps and frames, its crossbars, pillars, and bases;
the ark with its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain that screens it;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light with its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance to the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
the pegs of the tabernacle and the pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes;
the finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests."
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites withdrew from Moses' presence.
And everyone whose heart stirred him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought the LORD's offering for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
They came, both men and women; all who were willing in heart brought brooches, earrings, rings, and pendants—every kind of gold ornament—everyone presenting an offering of gold to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats' hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.
Everyone who could give an offering of silver or bronze brought it as the LORD's offering, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
And all the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats' hair.
The leaders brought the onyx stones and the other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece,
along with the spices and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
So every man and woman whose heart moved them brought something for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses; the Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.

versions.text: Every man and woman whose heart moved them to bring something for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses—the Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
versions.explanation: The current sentence leaves the opening subject dangling before the dash, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Restructuring keeps the sense of the Hebrew while giving the verse a clear, natural rhythm.

text: Then Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
and has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of craft,
to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,
to cut and set stones and to carve wood—to work in every kind of artistic craft.
And he has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.

He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers—masters of every craft and designers of artistic works.
